traceability.evidence:
Story linkage and implementation: - The core rule implementing this story is src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts. - Multiple JSDoc blocks explicitly reference the story and its requirements, e.g.: /** * Report an invalid @story annotation without applying a fix. * * @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md * @req REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT - Provide safe, minimal automatic fixes for common format issues */ - The main create(context) export is annotated with: * @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md * @req REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION * @req REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION and other related requirements, explicitly tying this rule to the story.
Core format specification and syntax validation (REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION, REQ-SYNTAX-VALIDATION, REQ-PATH-FORMAT, REQ-REQ-FORMAT): - src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-options.ts defines the canonical formats: - Story path pattern: function getDefaultStoryPattern(): RegExp { return /^docs\/stories\/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-DEV-[\w-]+\.story\.md$/; } This enforces relative paths under docs/stories with a .story.md extension, matching the story’s examples. - Requirement ID pattern: function getDefaultReqPattern(): RegExp { return /^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$/; } This matches the REQ-* format described in the story. - resolveOptions(...) wires these patterns into ResolvedAnnotationOptions (storyPattern, reqPattern, storyExample, reqExample), which valid-annotation-format.ts uses for validation. - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts: - validateStoryAnnotation(...) trims and collapses the value, then applies options.storyPattern to validate the @story path, reporting invalidStoryFormat when missing or malformed. - validateReqAnnotation(...) does the same for @req values with options.reqPattern, reporting invalidReqFormat when missing or malformed. - Program(...) in the rule’s create(...) walks all comments, finds @story and @req, and runs this validation logic, ensuring syntax is checked for all annotations detected via comments.
Multiline support and flexible parsing (REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT, REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING): - src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-format-internal.ts: - PendingAnnotation type and normalizeCommentLine(rawLine: string) abstract away JSDoc formatting, removing leading '*' and keeping @story/@req/@implements tokens even when they are not at the start of the line. - src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-utils.ts: - collapseAnnotationValue(value: string): string replaces all whitespace with a single empty string, effectively concatenating multi-line annotation values: return value.replace(/\s+/g, ""); - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts: - processComment(...) splits a comment into lines, normalizes each line, and uses processCommentLine(...) to manage a PendingAnnotation that can span multiple lines. - processCommentLine(...) appends continuation lines to pending.value and later finalizePendingAnnotation(...) passes the collapsed value into validateStoryAnnotation or validateReqAnnotation. - This behavior directly matches the story’s requirement to handle annotations split across multiple lines with flexible whitespace and JSDoc formatting.
Error specificity and user experience (REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY and UX acceptance criteria): - src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-utils.ts: - buildStoryErrorMessage(kind, value, options) returns human-readable messages with the offending path and an example: - Missing: "Missing story path for @story annotation. Expected a path like \"docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md\"." - Invalid: "Invalid story path \"\" for @story annotation. Expected a path like \"docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md\"." - buildReqErrorMessage(kind, value, options) similarly includes the bad ID and an example, plus a note on allowed characters. - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts meta.messages: - invalidStoryFormat, invalidReqFormat, and invalidImplementsFormat share a consistent prefix: "Invalid annotation format: {{details}}." and the details string is built as above, providing clear, specific, and actionable error messages per the story’s acceptance criteria.
Error handling and configuration robustness (Error Handling acceptance criterion): - src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-options.ts: - resolvePattern(...) attempts to construct RegExp from user-provided patterns. On failure, it pushes a stable error string via buildInvalidRegexError(field, pattern) into optionErrors and falls back to default patterns. - resolveOptions(...) collects these errors and updates a global resolvedDefaults, ensuring the rule always has valid patterns. - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts create(context): - const optionErrors = getOptionErrors(); - In the Program visitor, if optionErrors has entries, it reports them via messageId "invalidRuleConfiguration", but still validates comments using defaults. - This behavior satisfies graceful error handling: malformed config does not crash linting and is reported clearly.
Integration with existing rules (Integration acceptance criterion): - src/index.ts: - valid-annotation-format is included in RULE_NAMES and dynamically loaded: const RULE_NAMES = [ "require-story-annotation", "require-req-annotation", "require-branch-annotation", "valid-annotation-format", "valid-story-reference", "valid-req-reference", ] as const; - It is also mapped into TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES as a warning-level rule: "traceability/valid-annotation-format": "warn", - The plugin’s recommended and strict configs include this rule, ensuring it runs alongside the function and branch annotation rules described in earlier stories.
Tests and verification (Tested and passing criteria): - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts is explicitly tied to this story: - Header: /** * Tests for: docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md * @story docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md * @req REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION - Verify valid-annotation-format rule enforces annotation format syntax */ - Valid cases cover: - Single-line @story with a correctly formatted path (REQ-PATH-FORMAT). - Single-line @req with valid REQ-EXAMPLE format (REQ-REQ-FORMAT). - Block comments with both annotations on separate lines (REQ-FORMAT-SPECIFICATION). - Multi-line @story and @req values in block comments (REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT). - JSDoc-style comments with leading '*' and extra whitespace (REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING). - Invalid cases assert specific messageIds and details strings: - Missing story path, missing extension, invalid extension, and paths with '../' traversal (REQ-PATH-FORMAT, REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY). - Missing req identifier, invalid format, and whitespace-only IDs (REQ-REQ-FORMAT, REQ-ERROR-SPECIFICITY). - Multi-line invalid values, verifying that collapseAnnotationValue and syntax validation work correctly across lines (REQ-MULTILINE-SUPPORT, REQ-FLEXIBLE-PARSING). - Tests also cover configuration error handling (invalid regex patterns) and verify that configuration errors and subsequent annotation format errors are both reported in a controlled way. - Targeted Jest run for this test file: - Command (via tool): npx jest --ci --runInBand --verbose --testPathPatterns tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts - The command completed without any "Command failed" output or Jest errors, indicating all tests in this file passed. - Project test suite run through npm script: - Command (via tool): npm test -- --runInBand --verbose - Output: > eslint-plugin-traceability@1.0.5 test > jest --ci --bail --runInBand --verbose - No failures or stack traces were reported, so the full Jest suite (including the valid-annotation-format tests) passed.
Documentation alignment (Documentation acceptance criterion): - docs/stories/005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md includes explicit examples of valid and invalid annotations (missing extension, path traversal, invalid requirement IDs, missing identifiers). These scenarios directly correspond to the patterns enforced by getDefaultStoryPattern/getDefaultReqPattern and the cases covered in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts, showing that the implementation matches the documented format rules.
traceability.notes: This story defines a rule that validates the format and syntax of @story and @req annotations before any file/requirement existence checks. The implementation provides a dedicated valid-annotation-format ESLint rule, with shared helpers for options, normalization, and error message construction. It enforces clear patterns for story paths and requirement IDs, supports multi-line annotations and varied JSDoc comment formatting, and produces detailed, consistent error messages. Configuration errors for regex patterns are handled gracefully with explicit error messages and fallbacks, and the rule is integrated into the plugin’s rule set and configs. Comprehensive Jest tests explicitly reference this story and its requirements, verifying valid and invalid patterns, multiline behavior, error messages, and configuration handling; these tests, along with the full suite, run successfully. All acceptance criteria and listed requirements for story 005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION are satisfied.
